summary: Add a `getLogsByType(type: string)` query method to the existing `ConsoleLogger` class in `packages/saturday-core/src/utils/console-logger.ts` so that callers can retrieve only the captured console log entries matching a given type (e.g. `'error'`) instead of filtering the full `getLogs()` array by hand at every call site. This is a small, purely additive read-only method following the existing `getLogs()`/`getFormattedLogs()`/`clear()` style on an already-exported class — no new package, base class, layer boundary, or API surface is introduced.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: getLogsByType('error') returns only entries whose type is 'error'
examples: logs = [{type:'log',...}, {type:'error',...}, {type:'error',...}] → getLogsByType('error') returns the 2 entries with type 'error', in original capture order

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An unmatched type returns an empty array, never undefined
examples: getLogsByType('warning') on a logs array containing no 'warning' entries returns [] (Array.isArray === true, length 0), not undefined or null

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The method performs no I/O and does not mutate the captured logs
examples: Calling getLogsByType(...) does not change the length or contents of the array subsequently returned by getLogs(); no page/network/filesystem access occurs inside the method

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A unit test in packages/saturday-core/tests/utils/console-logger.spec.ts covers the match case and the empty-result case

proposedFitnessFunctions.property: getLogsByType is a pure, synchronous, non-mutating query (no I/O, no side effects on this.logs)
proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: code-reviewer inspection of the method body (must be a single synchronous Array.filter over this.logs, no async/await, no this.page.* calls, no reassignment of this.logs) plus the QA test asserting getLogs() is unchanged after a getLogsByType() call

outOfScope: Changes to getLogs(), getFormattedLogs(), or clear()
Changes to ConsoleLogger consumers (packages/saturday-cucumber/src/world/saturday-world.ts, hooks/setup.ts) — they construct/store the instance but have no getLogs().filter(...) call site to migrate
Barrel export changes in packages/saturday-core/src/index.ts — ConsoleLogger is already exported via `export * from './utils/console-logger'`
The separate apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/saturday-core/src/utils/console-logger.ts copy — spec names the packages/ path explicitly and this is not a symlink to it
Extracting the log entry shape into a named exported type (e.g. ConsoleLogEntry) — see Open Questions

Add unit tests for the match case and the empty-result (never-undefined) case per AC #4, reusing the existing mockPage/consoleListener harness

dataModelChanges.description: None — no persisted or transmitted data model changes; this reads the existing in-memory `logs` array shape ({type, text, location, timestamp}) unchanged

architecturalFlags: Architect not required — purely additive query method on an already-exported class, following the existing getLogs()/getFormattedLogs()/clear() pattern; no new package, base class, interface, or layer-boundary change.

No DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md update proposed — ConsoleLogger is Saturday framework test tooling (test-run infrastructure), not a business/product domain concept the dictionary governs; grepped DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md for 'Console'/'Logger'/'log entry' and found no existing entries to reconcile against.
Security-reviewer not required — no auth, input from untrusted external actors, network I/O, or trust-boundary crossing; the `type` argument is caller-supplied test code, not user input.

developer: In packages/saturday-core/src/utils/console-logger.ts, add `public getLogsByType(type: string) { return this.logs.filter((log) => log.type === type); }` immediately after the existing getLogs() method, matching its return-style (no explicit return type annotation, consistent with getLogs())
Do not modify setupConsoleListener, getFormattedLogs, or clear — this is an additive, read-only method
qa: Add test 'getLogsByType returns only entries matching the given type' to packages/saturday-core/tests/utils/console-logger.spec.ts: push 2+ log entries of differing types via the existing consoleListener mock harness, call getLogsByType('error'), assert the returned array contains only the matching entries in capture order

Add test 'getLogsByType returns an empty array, never undefined, for an unmatched type': call getLogsByType('warning') against logs with no matching entries (including the zero-logs case) and assert Array.isArray(result) === true and result.length === 0
Add an assertion (in either test or a dedicated one) that calling getLogsByType(...) does not mutate the array returned by a subsequent getLogs() call — covers AC #3's no-mutation requirement
techWriter: No package-level README exists for saturday-core and no docs/ files reference ConsoleLogger's public API today (confirmed via grep) — no doc update is required beyond this feature's own docs/features/console-log-filtering/ record
If the monorepo maintains a root or package-level CHANGELOG, add an entry noting the new ConsoleLogger.getLogsByType(type) method

edgeCases.case: logs array is empty (no console messages captured yet) when getLogsByType is called
edgeCases.handling: Array.prototype.filter on an empty array returns [], satisfying AC #2 with no special-casing needed

edgeCases.case: type argument is an empty string or a value that never appears in playwright's ConsoleMessage.type() output (e.g. 'trace', 'startGroup')
edgeCases.handling: Treated like any other unmatched type — exact string equality against log.type, returns [] rather than throwing or returning undefined

edgeCases.case: Multiple captured entries share the same type
edgeCases.handling: All matching entries are returned, preserving original capture (chronological) order, since filter preserves array order

edgeCases.case: Case sensitivity of the type argument vs. captured log.type
edgeCases.handling: Exact, case-sensitive equality only — no normalization. Playwright's ConsoleMessage.type() already returns consistently lowercase values ('log', 'error', 'warning', 'info', 'debug'), so this matches existing caller expectations without added complexity

openQuestions: The captured log entry shape ({type, text, location, timestamp}) is currently an inline anonymous type on the private `logs` field, and getLogsByType's return type will be inferred from the same inline shape. Now that two public methods (getLogs, getLogsByType) both surface this shape, should it be extracted into a named exported type (e.g. `ConsoleLogEntry`) for callers to reference in their own type annotations? Spec doesn't request this, and current scope treats it as out-of-scope, but flagging since it's the kind of thing that tends to get asked for immediately after this ships.
